facts.statement: Ruyangosaurus is a genus of titanosauriform sauropod dinosaur found in the Early Cretaceous Haoling Formation of China.
facts.quote: Ruyangosaurus (Ruyang County lizard) is a genus of titanosauriform sauropod dinosaur recovered from the Early Cretaceous Haoling Formation of China.

facts.statement: The type species Ruyangosaurus giganteus was described in 2009 by Lü Junchang and colleagues.
facts.quote: The type species is R. giganteus, described in 2009 by Lü Junchang et al.

facts.statement: In 2016, Gregory S. Paul estimated Ruyangosaurus reached a length of 30 meters and a weight of over 50 tonnes, classifying it as a 'mega-sauropod'.
facts.quote: In 2016 Gregory S. Paul gave a length of 30 meters (98 ft) and a weight of 50+ tonnes (55 short tons) - making it a 'mega-sauropod'.

facts.statement: Another estimate suggests Ruyangosaurus was about 35 meters long, based on a 207 cm femur and a 127 cm right tibia.
facts.quote: According to another estimate, Ruyangosaurus was probably about 35 meters (115 ft) long, as evidenced by its 207 cm long femur and 127 cm long right tibia.

facts.statement: In 2020, Molina-Perez and Larramendi provided a lower size estimate of 24.8 meters in length and 34 tonnes in weight.
facts.quote: In 2020 Molina-Perez and Larramendi gave a lower estimation of 24.8 meters (81.4 ft) and 34 tonnes (37.5 short tons).

facts.statement: Ruyangosaurus lived in the middle Cretaceous, approximately 95 million years ago during the Cenomanian, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, entre 95 millones de años, desde el Cenomaniense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Ruyangosaurus fossils were recovered from the Mangchuan Formation in Ruyang County, Henan Province, China.
facts.quote: Recuperado de la Formación Mangchuan, en el Condado de Ruyang, Provincia de Henan, China.

facts.statement: Ruyangosaurus is characterized by the shape of its vertebral laminae and a robust tibia measuring 127 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: Caracterizado por la forma de las láminas de sus vértebras y su robusta tibia de 127 centímetros de largo.

facts.statement: Ruyangosaurus giganteus is considered one of the largest sauropods in China, reaching around 30 meters in length and potentially sharing the family Lognkosauria with Argentinosaurus.
facts.quote: R. giganteus representa un nuevo dinosaurio gigante, capaz de compararse con Argentinosaurus, con el cual podría compartir la familia Lognkosauria y por mucho es el saurópodo más grande de China, con alrededor de 30 metros de largo.

facts.statement: The original describers assigned Ruyangosaurus to Andesauridae, but this family is no longer used because it is not monophyletic.
facts.quote: The describers of Ruyangosaurus assigned it to Andesauridae. However, Andesauridae is not monophyletic and, as such, is no longer used.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Ruyangosaurus is a somphospondyl or a non-titanosauriform macronarian closely related to Yunmenglong, as different phylogenetic datasets yield conflicting results.
facts.quote: However, not all phylogenetic analyses have supported its position as a somphospondyl. A phylogenetic dataset following the description of additional material for Ruyangosaurus to be a non-titanosauriform macronarian, closely related to Yunmenglong.

facts.statement: A smaller phylogenetic dataset based on additional material from the type locality found Ruyangosaurus to be a non-titanosauriform macronarian.
facts.quote: Un conjunto de datos filogenéticos más pequeño encontró que Ruyangosaurus es un macronario no titanosauriforme basado en material adicional de la localidad tipo.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Ruyangosaurus as Euhelopodidae.
Ruyangosaurus lived during the Aptian to Albian stages, between 121.4 and 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Albian (121.4 to 100.5 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Although originally thought to be from the early Late Cretaceous, Ruyangosaurus is now dated to the Aptian-Albian ages based on invertebrate and microfossil analysis.
rejected.quote: The horizon of Ruyangosaurus was originally described as being of 'early Late Cretaceous' age, but recent work has assigned it an Aptian-Albian Age based on fieldwork and analysis of invertebrate and microfossil assemblages.
